title: 18 Feeding behavior of naïve and adapted heifers grazing endophyte-infected or endophyte-free tall fescue pastures
content:
Abstract
Research has demonstrated that consumption of endophyte-infected tall fescue (E+TF) alters grazing behavior in beef cattle. Long-term, 24h monitoring of grazing and rumination behavior has not been reported on E+TF pastures. Our objective was to evaluate feeding behavior and performance in heifers adapted (FA) and naïve (FN) to E+TF when initially transitioning to pasture. We hypothesized that FN heifers grazing E+TF would spend less time grazing and ruminating compared to FA heifers and FN heifers grazing endophyte-free tall fescue (E-TF), resulting in less average daily gain (ADG). In May, yearling beef heifers from Kentucky (FA, n=15) and Montana (FN, n=30) were stratified by body weight and hair coat score into 9 pastures assigned to 1 of 3 treatments: FA on E+TF (FA-E+), FN on E+TF (FN-E+), or FN on E-TF (FN-E-). Heifers were weighed prior to the start of grazing and at the end of May (~31-d) to determine ADG. All heifers were outfitted with a Smart Rumen Bolus (Moonsyst, Cork, Ireland) and 2 heifers from each pasture were fitted with the RumiWatch System (RW) noseband sensors (Itin+Hoch GmbH, Liestal, Switzerland) for continuous monitoring of rumen temperature and feeding behavior, respectively. Data were analyzed using the mixed procedure of SAS (v.9.4) with contrasts to determine cattle source (FA-E+ vs FN-E+) and endophyte (FN-E+ vs FN-E-) effects. After the first 3-d where all groups were similar, FA-E+ heifers spent less time grazing than FN-E+ heifers (avg. 678 vs 746 min·d-1; p≤0.05) while FN-E+ and FN-E- were similar for the entire grazing period. Overall, FA-E+ heifers spent more time ruminating than FN-E+ (480 vs 423 min·d-1; p≤0.05). FN-E+ heifers also ruminated less than FN-E- heifers over the first 6-d of grazing (avg. 362 vs 408 min·d-1; p≤0.05) but were similar for the remainder of the period. During the grazing period, greater ADG was observed in FA-E+ (0.18±0.04 kg·day-1) than in FN-E+ (-0.27±0.04 kg·day-1, p≤0.05), and was also higher in FN-E- (0.00±0.04 kg·day-1) than FN-E+ (p≤0.05). Average THI (67.6) and rumen temperature (39.3°C) during May indicate that heat stress was not likely a contributing factor to differences observed. Contrary to our hypothesis, FN-E+ heifers spent more time grazing when compared to FA-E+ heifers. Feeding behaviors in FN heifers were similar for most of the grazing period indicating a cattle source effect on grazing adaptation. The combined feeding behavior observations of more grazing and less rumination time, in addition to lower ADG, in FN heifers suggests that FA heifers may be more efficient grazers in their natural environment. ADG differences between FN-E+ and FN-E- heifers in a thermoneutral environment suggest an endophyte effect. Future studies are needed to determine impacts of endophyte on feeding behavior and performance in heat stress conditions.
